title: 1991 AHSME Problem 15
statement: A circular table has exactly \(60\) chairs around it. There are \(N\) people seated at this table in such a way that the next person to be seated must sit next to someone. The smallest possible value of \(N\) is

solutions.text:
The condition says that every empty chair has an occupied neighbor, so no three consecutive chairs may all be empty. Therefore each occupied chair can account for at most itself and the two empty chairs following it, giving \(60\le3N\) and \(N\ge20.\) Repeating the pattern occupied-empty-empty around the table attains \(N=20.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: No empty chair can have both neighboring chairs empty
Between consecutive occupied chairs there can be at most two empty chairs
